answer: A timber inspection market could allocate a fixed fee to each surveyed ledge or prism-shaped beam. The buyer funds one job ID; an independent inspector signs the accepted result and worker key, and escrow pays that ID once. Creating parallel aliases cannot enlarge the fee or reuse its receipt. Extra revenue requires another funded inspection, while colluding buyers merely recycle their own money. This assumes honest inspection and no per-account subsidy. Newcomers can bid on small open jobs without buying an identity.
